title: Alvarez’s Rocket Launches Argentina Past Switzerland in World Cup Thriller
summary: Have you ever seen a soccer ball fly so fast it looks like a comet? That’s what happened when Julian Alvarez scored a stunning goal from 25 yards out in the 112th minute. His shot rocketed into the top corner, giving Argentina a 3-1 win over Switzerland in the World Cup quarterfinals on Saturday. The match was played at Kansas City Stadium, where Argentina took an early lead. Just 10 minutes in, Alexis Mac Allister headed in a perfect cross from Lionel Messi. But Switzerland fought back. Dan Ndoye tied the game in the 67th minute, tapping the ball in from close range. Then things got wild. Swiss star Breel Embolo got a second yellow card for diving — that means he pretended to be fouled — and had to leave the field. Switzerland was down to 10 players. Even so, Argentina couldn’t score again in regular time. Messi almost won it, but his chip shot was saved. The game went to extra time, and that’s when Alvarez stole the show. His long-range strike was so powerful the goalkeeper had no chance. As Switzerland pushed everyone forward, Argentina scored again. Lautaro Martinez finished a counterattack in the final seconds. Now Argentina faces England in the semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta. Only two countries have ever won back-to-back World Cups. Can Messi and Argentina make history? We’ll find out soon!
why_it_matters: Like a last-minute goal in your own game, this story shows that even when things are tough, a single moment of skill and determination can change everything.

background_read: Argentina is a South American country with a very strong soccer tradition; they have won the World Cup three times. The World Cup, held every four years, is the biggest soccer tournament on Earth. A team winning back-to-back titles has only happened twice before—once by Italy in the 1930s and again by Brazil in the 1950s and 60s.
Article_Structure: WHO: Julian Alvarez, Lionel Messi, Alexis Mac Allister, Dan Ndoye, Breel Embolo, Lautaro Martinez
WHAT: Argentina beat Switzerland 3-1 after extra time in the World Cup quarterfinals with late goals from Alvarez and Martinez.
WHY: Switzerland had a player sent off (red card) for a second yellow, but Argentina still needed a moment of magic from Alvarez to break the tie and advance to the semifinals.

perspectives.description: Fans are thrilled that their team survived a hard fight and that their young star Alvarez came through with such a powerful game-winning goal.
Supporters feel proud of their team's effort, especially after being reduced to ten men. They are disappointed that a close game slipped away so late.
People who love the sport enjoyed an exciting, back-and-forth match with a wonderful long-distance strike that will be remembered for a long time.
